Class AlgoRebalancingService

java.lang.Object
grafioschtrader.service.AlgoRebalancingService
@Service public class AlgoRebalancingService extends Object
Compares an AlgoTop against the holdings it describes and says what would restore the configured allocation.

The service decides, it does not act. A live evaluation writes the plan and raises a notification; the portfolio is changed by the user, through the ordinary transaction path. Historical replay and forward scenarios will drive the same calculation with their own market observations, which is why the plan is built from a supplied snapshot rather than from whatever the database happens to hold at the moment of the call.

Two things are easy to get wrong here and are therefore stated once. The hierarchy stores parent-relative weights, so a bucket at 50% of a 48.2% ceiling is 24.1% of equity and not 50% of anything the report shows; every percentage this service produces has already been resolved against total net equity. And the quantity being allocated is gross exposure, not net position value: a short position and a margin position contribute their notional to the budget while contributing only their unrealised result to equity.

      The last completed day, which is the newest day a closing valuation may be asked for. AlgoHistoricalValuationService.validateDate(LocalDate) rejects today, because an unfinished day has no closing price and the plan would compare against a moving target.

    • plan

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public RebalancingPlan plan(Integer idTenant, AlgoTop algoTop, LocalDate valuationDate, Locale locale)
      Builds the plan of one AlgoTop against the closing state of a day, reading prices from the historical repository.
      Parameters:
      idTenant - tenant whose positions are compared; for a live evaluation the tenant that owns the AlgoTop
      algoTop - the hierarchy that defines the targets
      valuationDate - completed day whose closing holdings and prices are used
      locale - language of the bucket labels; nothing that reaches the database depends on it
      Returns:
      the resolved comparison
      Throws:
      DataViolationException - if the AlgoTop carries no rebalancing configuration, its weights do not add up, or the day cannot be valued

    • plan

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public RebalancingPlan plan(Integer idTenant, AlgoTop algoTop, LocalDate valuationDate, Locale locale, LocalDate lastRebalancedOn)
      Builds the plan against a caller supplied date of the previous redeployment.

      The stored plan carries the day of the last live checkpoint, which is the right answer for a live evaluation and the wrong one for a historical replay: a replay walks its own timeline, and asking the stored plan when it last rebalanced would either make every replayed day due or none of them. A replay therefore remembers the day it last redeployed and passes it in here.

      Parameters:
      idTenant - tenant whose positions are compared
      algoTop - the hierarchy that defines the targets
      valuationDate - completed day whose closing holdings and prices are used
      locale - language of the bucket labels
      lastRebalancedOn - day of the previous redeployment, or null to read it from the stored plan; a null value together with no stored plan makes the interval due, as it does for a hierarchy that was never evaluated
      Returns:
      the resolved comparison

    • hasRebalancingStrategy

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public boolean hasRebalancingStrategy(AlgoTop algoTop)
      Whether the hierarchy carries a rebalancing strategy at all. A caller that treats an unconfigured hierarchy as an ordinary case asks this first, so that everything plan(Integer, AlgoTop, LocalDate, Locale) still refuses is a real impediment worth reporting rather than a configuration decision to be passed over in silence.
      Parameters:
      algoTop - the hierarchy to look at
      Returns:
      true when a rebalancing strategy is defined on its top level

    • isCheckpointDue

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public boolean isCheckpointDue(Integer idTenant, AlgoTop algoTop, LocalDate valuationDate, LocalDate lastRebalancedOn)
      Whether the allocation of this hierarchy is to be compared on that day at all.

      This exists separately from plan(Integer, AlgoTop, LocalDate, Locale) because it is the cheap half of the question. Building a plan values every position and reads a closing quote per instrument and per currency pair; asking the interval first means a run of a thousand days with four redeployments per year pays for twelve of those valuations instead of a thousand. A caller that already holds a plan reads RebalancingPlan.periodicDue() instead.

      Parameters:
      idTenant - tenant whose positions would be compared
      algoTop - the hierarchy that defines the targets
      valuationDate - the day in question
      lastRebalancedOn - day of the previous redeployment, or null to read it from the stored plan; a null value together with no stored plan makes the checkpoint due, which is how an environment that has never been rebalanced reaches its targets on its first day
      Returns:
      true when the interval has elapsed
      Throws:
      DataViolationException - if the hierarchy carries no rebalancing configuration

    • hasDueRebalancing

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public boolean hasDueRebalancing()
      Whether any AlgoTop still owes an evaluation today. Deliberately cheap: it reads the run day of the stored plans and values nothing, because it runs on the five minute scan that only decides whether to enqueue the real work.

    • persist

      public void persist(RebalancingPlan plan)
      Replaces the previous plan of this AlgoTop, so the table holds one plan rather than the union of two.

      The plan is replaced on every daily evaluation, so the start of the periodic interval cannot be read off the run day of the stored rows. A plan that is a checkpoint records its valuation day, traded or not; every plan in between carries the last checkpoint over from the rows it replaces. Without this the interval restarted each day and never elapsed again after the first evaluation.

      Parameters:
      plan - the plan to store
